correctness.rationale: For j≤n the recursion partitions Z_n into 2^(n−j) identical literal Z_j blocks separated by single symbols above j. Each block contains exactly one j. Any nonempty factor whose largest letter is j must lie wholly within one such block, and its same relative occurrence in any other such block crosses that block's j. This proves the sufficiency for any selected representative of each letter, including j=1 and j=n; the singleton factors give necessity. Choosing independent nonempty subsets of the symbol classes gives the complete polynomial, evaluation at t=1 gives the total, and the lowest exponent n and its coefficient give the optimal family and count. Inspected the frozen checks of coverage masks and centered neighbourhoods; those finite computations are supplementary and the uploaded code was not run.

evidence: The older factor theorem states that a word on {1,…,k} is a factor of Z_k iff it satisfies the interleaving condition after each threshold deletion.

For f with maximum j≤n, the same conditions up to j apply without change. Each position j in Z_n belongs to the center of a copy of Z_j. Since f contains j, its occurrence in each copy includes its center.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus any set hitting each symbol covers every factor; the converse is a singleton test. With 2^(n−j) positions in class j from the recursion, selecting independent nonempty subsets mechanically gives the full cardinality polynomial and all minimum/total counts. There is no additional factor occurrence theorem or independent enumerative step needed.

value.rationale: The attractor interpretation is a useful observation, but the exact family and all its coefficients arise by applying the standard hitting definition to the already characterized factors and making routine independent subset choices. There is no separate useful new invariant or boundary result in the frozen claim. A binary or substituted-word extension would be a different problem, not a supported repair.
